title: Types of AI
tagline: Where does an AI's skill come from? Compare written rules, learned scores, and a neural network on one board.
card_blurb: Compare written rules, a learned value table, and a neural network on one tic-tac-toe board. Inspect the network’s actual weights, explore other model families, and distinguish the model from how it learns.
description: **Types of AI** compares **1a Symbolic AI (GOFAI)**, **1b Value table**, and **1c Neural Network** on one tic-tac-toe board. **1d Other model types** introduces additional families, while the separate **How they learn** tab explains supervised, unsupervised, self-supervised, reinforcement, and semi-supervised learning. The symbolic opponent follows eight written rules; the table learns position values through reinforcement; a feedforward network uses supervised learning to approximate frozen estimates from a fresh 20,000-game table learner. The network inspector shows real layers, connection weights, biases, and changes from initialization. Exhaustive policy checks support claims about the rules and table. Training/held-out errors measure agreement with the frozen teacher; playing results are measured separately, with no automatic unbeatable claim for the network. During play the network calculates its own scores without consulting the teacher. Ultimate tic-tac-toe remains an optional missing-inputs extension. Runs offline with Guide, Settings, presenter notes and a printable guide.
